prompt.context: Your client is a large global bank, Bank of FinTeck, and in 2012 it generated $30 Billion in revenue, ranking 3rd among global banks. However, now in 2015, the bank's revenue has remained stagnant over the last 3 years, and seen its reputation deteriorate.
prompt.question: What should this bank do to inject growth into the business, and avoid declining year over year revenues?

clarifying_info.q: What is the revenue growth target?
clarifying_info.a: The client is looking for 5% revenue growth over 3 years, in aggregate.

clarifying_info.q: What business units does the bank operate?
clarifying_info.a: Its core business units are retail, commercial, and investment bank products and services.

clarifying_info.q: How does Commodities Trading generate revenue?
clarifying_info.a: Through broker fees and trade transaction fees.

clarifying_info.q: How does Investment Services generate revenue?
clarifying_info.a: It provides services across the investment lifecycle — trading, distribution of funds, clearing, settlement, and other fee-based back-office services.

clarifying_info.q: How does Wealth Management charge clients?
clarifying_info.a: It charges a 125 bps portfolio management fee. It is a very localized industry where relationships are the most important factor.

clarifying_info.q: How does Credit Card generate revenue?
clarifying_info.a: Through merchant fees, issuing fees, and interest.

clarifying_info.q: Does Bank of FinTeck currently have a Credit Card business?
clarifying_info.a: No, the client does not currently have a Credit Card business, which would require a large investment to build.

exhibits.title: 2015 Market Size by Product/Service
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing 2015 market size (in $B) across four product/service categories — Commodities Trading, Investment Services, Wealth Management, and Credit Card — broken down by Bank of FinTeck, Competitor 1, Competitor 2, Competitor 3, and Other.

data.Wealth Management: roughly $12B total market, appears highly fragmented
data.Bank of FinTeck share: visible but not dominant in any category

exhibits.title: Forecasted Revenue with New Technology (2016F–2018F)
exhibits.shows: A table showing three-year forecasted figures for Transaction Settlements volume and fee, FX Transactions volume and fee, Technology Capital Investment, Other Costs and Overhead, and a bottom-line Profit figure — all in thousands.

framework: Identify the root cause: revenue stagnation (price x quantity) vs. cost growth — confirm this is a revenue problem
Understand the bank's business units: retail, commercial, investment banking products and services
Assess industry trends: new regulation compliance, disruptive technologies, competitive dynamics
Evaluate revenue drivers by segment: products offered, fees charged, customer base, market share
Identify growth levers: new products/services, geographic expansion, pricing, technology-driven efficiency and capacity
Prioritize by market size, competitive position, barriers to entry, and required investment

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, which of the four products/services should Bank of FinTeck invest in as its primary growth driver?
questions.guidance: Candidate should eliminate Commodities Trading immediately due to its small market size. Credit Card should be deprioritized because the bank has no existing business there, requiring a large greenfield build. Wealth Management, though fragmented, has very high barriers to entry due to its localized, relationship-driven nature. Investment Services is the best option: sizable market, existing presence, and fewer barriers. A great candidate also notes that 5% revenue growth on $30B = $1.5B target and relates this to each market's size to validate the choice.

math.setup: Revenue growth target = 5% of $30B over 3 years
steps: Investment Services total market ~$15B — meaningful headroom
Commodities Trading market ~$3B — too small to generate $1.5B incremental
Credit Card ~$18B but no existing business base; high build cost
Wealth Management ~$12B but relationship/localization barriers limit growth
math.answer: Investment Services is the recommended focus; it is the only option combining sufficient market size, existing bank presence, and manageable barriers to entry.

questions.prompt: Bank of FinTeck's Investment Services used to be the #1 firm but has lost ground. What can it do to reclaim the #1 position? (Brainstorm — customer acquisition and marketing are off the table; demand is not an issue.)
questions.guidance: Guide away from marketing/cross-selling and pure pricing strategies (significant pricing pressure from competition). Strong answers cover: operational efficiency improvements, new/innovative service offerings (e.g., technology-enabled speed), product differentiation, talent/capability investment, geographic or segment expansion within Investment Services, and technology as a differentiator. A great candidate arrives at technology-driven settlement speed as an innovation lever without being told.

questions.prompt: The client wants to implement a new technology that increases settlement speed for standard and FX transactions, allowing it to process more transactions and grow market share. Using Exhibit 2, determine whether the client will meet its 5% revenue growth target.
questions.guidance: Candidate must recognize that Profit in the exhibit already has costs deducted; to get Revenue, add back Technology Capital Investment and Other Costs & Overhead. The shortcut is: Revenue = Profit + Costs. Candidate should also remember that the current Investment Services revenue can be estimated at ~$3B from Exhibit 1. The growth target is $1.5B over 3 years. Candidates should then check cumulative incremental revenue vs. $1.5B target.

math.setup: Current IS revenue ≈ $3B (estimated from Exhibit 1 Bank of FinTeck bar). Target: +$1.5B over 3 years (5% of $30B).
math.answer: Yes, the client meets its 5% revenue growth target with $1.56B in incremental Investment Services revenue over 3 years, slightly exceeding the $1.5B goal.

brainstorming.prompt: Bank of FinTeck's Investment Services has been operating since inception but lost its #1 position due to lack of investment and increased competition. What can the bank do to reclaim the top spot? (Customer acquisition and marketing strategies are excluded — demand is not the issue.)

categories.name: Operational Efficiency
ideas: Streamline back-office processing to reduce cost per transaction
Reduce error rates and rework through process standardization

categories.name: Technology & Innovation
ideas: Implement faster settlement technology (real-time or near-real-time)
Invest in FX processing automation to handle higher volumes
Leverage APIs to integrate with client systems seamlessly

categories.name: Product & Service Expansion
ideas: Launch new fee-based back-office services (e.g., fund administration, custody)
Expand into adjacent investment lifecycle services not currently offered
Develop white-label services for smaller banks
Create bundled service packages to increase revenue per client

categories.name: Talent & Capability
ideas: Hire specialized talent in technology and investment operations
Build or acquire proprietary expertise in high-growth asset classes
Create a center of excellence for investment services best practices

categories.name: Pricing Strategy
ideas: Introduce tiered pricing based on transaction volume
Differentiate pricing for premium speed/reliability SLAs
Bundle services to reduce churn and increase wallet share

recommendation: Proceed with implementing the new settlement speed technology in Investment Services
The technology investment generates $1.56B in incremental revenue over three years, narrowly meeting the $1.5B (5%) growth target
Investment Services is the right vehicle: existing presence, sufficient market size, and addressable competitive gap
risks: The target is met only narrowly ($1.56B vs. $1.5B), leaving no margin for execution shortfalls or cost overruns
Technology implementation risk: delays or failures in the new system could disrupt existing settlement operations
Competitors may respond with similar technology investments, eroding first-mover advantage
The $150M Year 1 capital outlay is significant; if revenue ramps more slowly than forecast, payback period extends
Reputation deterioration mentioned upfront may require separate remediation effort beyond the technology fix
next_steps: Conduct detailed technology vendor selection and build-vs-buy analysis
Pilot the new settlement system on a subset of transactions before full rollout
Develop a risk mitigation and contingency plan for implementation delays
Monitor competitor responses and refine pricing strategy accordingly
Assess whether other business units (retail, commercial) need parallel growth initiatives to de-risk reliance on a single product line
